        {
            "id": "70fd9949-616d-47c0-ac5a-0bdbf04896de",
            "author": {
                "role": "assistant",
                "name": null,
                "metadata": {}
            },
            "create_time": 1792071885.446964,
            "update_time": 1792071916.553789,
            "content": {
                "content_type": "text",
                "parts": [
                    "# Elite X, Sector 10, Greater Noida West: 3BHK buying guide\n\nMy initial view: **Elite X is worth investigating, but I would not book it without resolving three things first: the all-inclusive price, the possession timeline, and whether its location makes sense for your daily life.**\n\nFor your situation, this isn't just an investment decision. You're looking for a 3BHK for your family, with a budget of around ₹2 crore, a commute to Sector 63, nearby schools, good open spaces, and a relatively new society. You also need the home within two years, which makes possession risk particularly important.\n\nElite X needs to be judged against those requirements, not just its advertised amenities or apartment size.\n\n## 1. What exactly is Elite X?\n\n<AsyncImageGroup query={[\"Elite X Sector 10 Greater Noida West official residential project exterior render\",\"Elite X Greater Noida West apartment interior floor plan brochure\",\"Elite X Sector 10 Greater Noida West landscape amenities master plan\"]} aspectRatio=\"5:4\" layout=\"bento\" size=\"lg\"/>\n\n<text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Project visuals are illustrative marketing imagery, not proof of completed construction.</text>\n\nThe project is being developed by Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd., associated with Elite Group, at Plot GH-03A, Sector 10, Greater Noida West. It is an under-construction residential development. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search0\",\"turn554236search1\"]}/>\n\n| Detail | What the available records indicate |\n|---|---|\n| Developer | Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd. |\n| UP RERA number | UPRERAPRJ916631/02/2024 |\n| RERA registration | 24 February 2024 |\n| RERA completion date | 12 December 2028 |\n| Project land | Approximately 5.44 acres |\n| Buildings | Six residential towers plus a commercial component in the RERA records |\n| Configurations | 3BHK, 3BHK with study, 4BHK |\n| Advertised apartment sizes | Approximately 1,800–2,110 sq ft for the 3BHK variants |\n| Indicative starting price | Around ₹2.10 crore on the developer's website |\n\nSources: <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search0\",\"turn554236search1\",\"turn554236search3\",\"turn554236search16\"]}/>\n\nOne important point: project websites and property portals sometimes report different numbers of towers and apartments. The registered plans and approved revisions should take precedence over marketing summaries.\n\nYou can check the registration directly on the <Entity value=\"UP RERA\" category=\"organization\" disambig=\"Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority\"/> website: <Link url=\"https://www.up-rera.in/\" title=\"Official UP RERA portal\"/>. Search for the exact registration number above.\n\n## 2. Is the 3BHK actually spacious?\n\nThis is one of the strongest reasons to consider Elite X, but be careful about the area being advertised.\n\n<box border radius=\"xl\" padding={4} gap={3}>\n  <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Example 3BHK listing</text>\n  <title size=\"2xl\" color=\"default\">1,800 sq ft</title>\n  <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Advertised super built-up area</text>\n  <divider/>\n  <row align=\"center\">\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      <title size=\"lg\">~968 sq ft</title>\n      <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Carpet area shown by a property-data portal for one configuration</text>\n    </box>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      <title size=\"lg\">~54%</title>\n      <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Carpet-to-super-area ratio for that example</text>\n    </box>\n  </row>\n  <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Area figures vary by unit and tower. Obtain the exact unit's RERA carpet area and approved plan before comparing prices. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search3\",\"turn554236search18\"]}/></text>\n</box>\n\nA 1,800 sq ft super-area flat is not the same as having 1,800 sq ft of usable indoor space. Super area includes a share of common areas, whereas carpet area measures the usable internal floor area as defined under RERA.\n\nBefore booking, ask for:\n\n- The exact carpet area of your selected unit.\n- The room dimensions, not just the total area.\n- The usable kitchen and utility area.\n- Balcony dimensions and whether furniture will fit comfortably.\n- The location of columns, shafts and structural walls.\n- The orientation of the living room and bedrooms.\n\n**My advice:** compare the actual carpet area of Elite X against ready-to-move 3BHKs in Noida. A larger advertised number alone does not make it a better flat.\n\n## 3. Price: can it fit your ₹2 crore budget?\n\nThe advertised starting price on the developer's website is around ₹2.10 crore. Other property portals have shown different figures, including lower base-price estimates. These are not necessarily comparable because unit, floor, view, payment plan and included charges can differ. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search1\",\"turn554236search3\",\"turn554236search6\"]}/>\n\nFor your budget, the relevant figure is the **total amount payable to get possession**, not the base price.\n\nHere's how a hypothetical negotiation would affect your position.\n\n<box border radius=\"xl\" padding={3} gap={3}>\n  {@body const [base,setBase] = DIL.useState(185)}\n  {@body const [charges,setCharges] = DIL.useState(10)}\n  {@body const [interiors,setInteriors] = DIL.useState(5)}\n  {@body const [budget,setBudget] = DIL.useState(200)}\n  <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Adjust the figures below. Amounts are in ₹ lakh.</text>\n  <box gap={1}>\n    <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n      <label>Negotiated base price</label>\n      <title size=\"md\" color=\"default\">₹{base} lakh</title>\n    </row>\n    <slider min={165} max={215} step={1} value={base} onChange={setBase} marks={[{\"value\":165,\"label\":\"₹1.65 Cr\"},{\"value\":190,\"label\":\"₹1.90 Cr\"},{\"value\":215,\"label\":\"₹2.15 Cr\"}]}/>\n  </box>\n  <box gap={1}>\n    <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n      <label>Other charges and taxes</label>\n      <title size=\"md\" color=\"default\">₹{charges} lakh</title>\n    </row>\n    <slider min={0} max={30} step={1} value={charges} onChange={setCharges} marks={[{\"value\":0,\"label\":\"₹0\"},{\"value\":15,\"label\":\"₹15L\"},{\"value\":30,\"label\":\"₹30L\"}]}/>\n  </box>\n  <box gap={1}>\n    <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n      <label>Interiors and moving costs</label>\n      <title size=\"md\" color=\"default\">₹{interiors} lakh</title>\n    </row>\n    <slider min={0} max={15} step={1} value={interiors} onChange={setInteriors} marks={[{\"value\":0,\"label\":\"₹0\"},{\"value\":8,\"label\":\"₹8L\"},{\"value\":15,\"label\":\"₹15L\"}]}/>\n  </box>\n  <box gap={1}>\n    <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n      <label>Your total budget</label>\n      <title size=\"md\" color=\"default\">₹{budget} lakh</title>\n    </row>\n    <slider min={180} max={240} step={5} value={budget} onChange={setBudget} marks={[{\"value\":180,\"label\":\"₹1.80 Cr\"},{\"value\":210,\"label\":\"₹2.10 Cr\"},{\"value\":240,\"label\":\"₹2.40 Cr\"}]}/>\n  </box>\n  <divider/>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <box gap={1}>\n      <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Estimated total</text>\n      <title size=\"2xl\" color=\"default\">₹{(base+charges+interiors).toFixed(1)} lakh</title>\n    </box>\n    <badge color={base+charges+interiors<=budget?\"success\":\"danger\"}>{base+charges+interiors<=budget?\"Within budget\":\"Over budget\"}</badge>\n  </row>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Difference from budget</text>\n    <title size=\"md\" color={base+charges+interiors<=budget?\"success\":\"danger\"}>{base+charges+interiors-budget<0?\"−\": \"+\"}₹{Math.abs(base+charges+interiors-budget).toFixed(1)} lakh</title>\n  </row>\n  <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">This is a planning calculator, not a verified Elite X quotation. It does not calculate taxes automatically. Actual GST applicability, stamp duty, registration, parking, maintenance deposits, other builder charges and interior costs must be confirmed separately.</text>\n</box>\n\nFor a property under construction, GST treatment depends on the applicable rules and transaction circumstances. Stamp duty and registration costs also depend on the applicable state rules and buyer details. Do not assume that a quoted base price includes these items.\n\n**My pricing stance:** if your ₹2 crore ceiling is firm and includes all costs, a quoted base price of ₹1.85 crore is already tight. At the advertised starting price of ₹2.10 crore, Elite X is unlikely to fit without a materially different offer or a higher budget.\n\nAsk the sales team for a dated, signed cost sheet for the exact unit. Don't rely on a broker's WhatsApp total.\n\n## 4. Possession and construction risk\n\nThis is the biggest concern for you.\n\nThe official UP RERA record lists **12 December 2028** as the declared completion date. That is later than your preferred two-year window, which runs to approximately October 2028. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search0\",\"turn554236search4\"]}/>\n\n<box border radius=\"xl\" padding={3} gap={3}>\n  <row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n    <icon name=\"calendar-clock\" size=\"xl\" color=\"warning\"/>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      **Your target: October 2028**\n\n      <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">You want a home within two years of October 2026.</text>\n    </box>\n  </row>\n  <divider/>\n  <row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n    <icon name=\"calendar\" size=\"xl\" color=\"danger\"/>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      **Elite X's RERA date: 12 December 2028**\n\n      <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">The declared completion date is roughly two months beyond your target, before allowing for any further delay or the time needed for handover and fit-out.</text>\n    </box>\n  </row>\n</box>\n\nA RERA completion date is not a guarantee that you will be able to move in that day. You need to distinguish between construction completion, the required occupancy certificate, the developer's possession offer and the actual handover of your apartment.\n\nA third-party compilation of the project's quarterly progress reports lists construction progress at approximately 30.21% for April–June 2026. This is a historical reported figure, not a verified October 2026 site inspection. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search4\"]}/>\n\nThat makes a fresh progress check essential. Ask for:\n\n- The latest quarterly progress report filed with UP RERA.\n- Current tower-wise construction status, including your chosen tower.\n- The sanctioned completion schedule and remaining construction milestones.\n- The expected date for occupancy certification and handover.\n- The agreement's delay-compensation clause and refund provisions.\n- The status of approvals, construction finance and any project encumbrances.\n\n**My recommendation:** if moving in within two years is a hard requirement, I would favour a completed property with the occupancy certificate, unless Elite X can offer a legally credible possession schedule that meets your deadline. A sales representative's verbal promise is not enough.\n\n## 5. Location and daily commute\n\n<AsyncImage query=\"Elite X GH-03A Sector 10 Greater Noida West location map NH 9 road connectivity\" aspectRatio=\"16:9\" width=\"100%\"/>\n\nElite X is in Sector 10, Greater Noida West, also known as Noida Extension. The developer markets it as having road connectivity to NH-9 and the wider Noida–Delhi region. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search1\",\"turn554236search6\"]}/>\n\nFor your office in Sector 63, Noida, the practical question is whether the daily drive is acceptable at peak hours. The distance on a map is not enough; the approach roads, junctions, bottlenecks and traffic direction matter.\n\nBefore committing, do this test:\n\n1. Drive from the actual project entrance to your office around 8:30–9:30 AM.\n2. Repeat the return trip around 6–7:30 PM.\n3. Check whether your route depends on a road improvement or transport link that is still proposed.\n4. Repeat the drive on a weekday, not just a Sunday.\n\nI would not make a purchase decision based on an advertised travel time or a future metro promise. Confirm operational transport options and the actual commute.\n\n## 6. Schools, hospitals and everyday facilities\n\nSector 10 and the wider Greater Noida West area have established residential and social infrastructure, although the quality and convenience of each facility need to be assessed individually.\n\n<box gap={3}>\n  <row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n    <AsyncImage query=\"Sarvottam International School Sector 10 Greater Noida West campus\" aspectRatio=\"4:5\" maxWidth=\"112px\"/>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      **<Entity ref=\"turn554236business1\" value=\"Sarvottam International School\"/>**\n\n      A school campus in Sector 10. Check the exact grades offered, current admissions, transport route and fees.\n    </box>\n  </row>\n  <divider color=\"subtle\"/>\n  <row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n    <AsyncImage query=\"Delhi World Public School Noida Extension Knowledge Park V campus\" aspectRatio=\"4:5\" maxWidth=\"112px\"/>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      **<Entity ref=\"turn554236business4\" value=\"Delhi World Public School, Noida Extension\"/>**\n\n      Another school option in Knowledge Park V. Confirm the relevant campus for your child's grade and its actual commute from the apartment.\n    </box>\n  </row>\n  <divider color=\"subtle\"/>\n  <row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n    <AsyncImage query=\"KDSG Super Speciality Hospital Sector 10 Greater Noida West exterior\" aspectRatio=\"4:5\" maxWidth=\"112px\"/>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      **<Entity ref=\"turn554236business0\" value=\"KDSG Super-Speciality Hospital\"/>**\n\n      Located in Sector 10. Check the departments, emergency facilities and services currently available.\n    </box>\n  </row>\n  <divider color=\"subtle\"/>\n  <row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n    <AsyncImage query=\"Ace City Square shopping complex Greater Noida West\" aspectRatio=\"4:5\" maxWidth=\"112px\"/>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      **<Entity value=\"Ace City Square\" category=\"point_of_interest\" location=\"Greater Noida West, Uttar Pradesh\" disambig=\"Shopping and retail complex\"/>**\n\n      A shopping option in the wider area. Verify the route, current stores and everyday essentials before treating it as your regular mall.\n    </box>\n  </row>\n</box>\n\nThese are area-level options, not a guarantee of a particular journey time or walking distance. Visit at school opening and closing times, and inspect the approach roads and pedestrian access.\n\n<MapWidgetV2 title=\"Elite X and nearby facilities\" points={[{\"id\":\"elite\",\"name\":\"Elite X\",\"address\":\"Plot GH-03A, Sector 10, Greater Noida West, Uttar Pradesh\",\"icon\":\"🏠\"},{\"ref\":\"turn554236business1\",\"icon\":\"🎓\"},{\"ref\":\"turn554236business4\",\"icon\":\"🎓\"},{\"ref\":\"turn554236business0\",\"icon\":\"🏥\"}]} show_route={false} carousel={{\"visibility\":\"hidden\"}}/>\n\n## 7. Open space, amenities and density\n\nElite X is marketed as a 5.44-acre project with approximately 69% open area, along with a swimming pool, fitness facilities, landscaped areas and other community amenities. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search1\",\"turn554236search2\"]}/>\n\nThat sounds attractive for family living. But there are three things I would check before treating it as a genuine advantage.\n\n- **Usable greens:** does the open area include landscaped podiums, circulation areas, setbacks or spaces that cannot be used freely?\n- **Density:** the RERA-derived project data indicates hundreds of apartments across multiple high-rise towers. Check the actual number of units per floor, lifts per tower and expected parking demand. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search3\",\"turn554236search4\"]}/>\n- **Maintenance:** ask for the estimated monthly maintenance rate per square foot, the services covered, and the proposed sinking fund or maintenance deposit.\n\nVisit the site and ask to see the approved master plan. Look for the distance between towers, afternoon shade, road noise, the location of the commercial area and whether the main greens are visible from the apartment you intend to buy.\n\nDo not assume that a large open-area percentage automatically means more quiet, privacy or usable garden space.\n\n## 8. Is Elite Group a reliable builder?\n\nThe developer behind Elite X is Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd. Elite Group's marketing materials identify earlier projects including Elite Homz in Sector 77 and Elite Golfgreens in Sector 79, Noida. <Cite refs={[\"turn554236search1\",\"turn554236search16\"]}/>\n\nThat gives you projects to investigate, but it does not establish the builder's delivery record or construction quality.\n\nBefore paying a booking amount, investigate:\n\n- **Possession history:** when were earlier projects actually handed over compared with their promised dates?\n- **Construction quality:** inspect completed buildings, common areas, basements, lifts, plumbing, waterproofing and finishing.\n- **Resident feedback:** speak directly to residents and maintenance staff, rather than relying exclusively on online ratings.\n- **Legal disputes:** check for pending material litigation, regulatory orders and land-related issues.\n- **Financial health:** have a property lawyer or qualified professional review the promoter, project charges, encumbrances and relevant disclosures.\n\nA registered project is not automatically free of legal or delivery risks. Equally, the existence of a complaint is not proof of wrongdoing. Look for documented evidence and patterns.\n\n## 9. Legal and financial checks before booking\n\nUse this as your booking checklist.\n\n{@body const checks = [\n{section:\"RERA and approvals\",items:[\"Verify the current RERA registration and all approved revisions.\",\"Review the sanctioned building plan and the exact tower and unit.\",\"Check the latest quarterly progress report and declared completion date.\"]},\n{section:\"Title and agreement\",items:[\"Have an independent property lawyer review land title, lease or ownership documents, and encumbrances.\",\"Read the builder-buyer agreement, possession terms, cancellation clauses and delay compensation.\",\"Check whether the advertised layout and specifications match the approved documents.\"]},\n{section:\"Money and payment\",items:[\"Get a complete written cost sheet, including taxes and every additional charge.\",\"Confirm the construction-linked payment schedule and due dates.\",\"Verify the RERA-designated collection account and the appropriate payment instructions.\",\"Check loan eligibility, lender approval and the consequences of construction delays.\"]},\n{section:\"Apartment and handover\",items:[\"Inspect the exact unit's carpet area, orientation, floor and view.\",\"Confirm parking allocation, maintenance charges and promised amenities in writing.\",\"Verify occupancy certification and all applicable handover documents before taking possession.\"]}\n]}\n{@body const [done,setDone] = DIL.useState([])}\n<box border radius=\"xl\" padding={3} gap={3}>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <title size=\"lg\">Booking due diligence</title>\n    <badge>{done.length}/{checks.reduce((n,s)=>n+s.items.length,0)} checked</badge>\n  </row>\n  <box background=\"surface-tertiary\" radius=\"full\" height=\"5px\" clip>\n    <box background=\"surface-inverted\" radius=\"full\" height=\"5px\" width={`${100*done.length/checks.reduce((n,s)=>n+s.items.length,0)}%`}/>\n  </box>\n  {#each checks as section}\n    <box key={section.section} gap={2}>\n      <text weight=\"medium\">{section.section}</text>\n      {#each section.items as item}\n        <checkbox key={item} checked={done.includes(item)} onChange={v=>setDone(old=>v?[...old,item]:old.filter(x=>x!==item))} lineThrough={false}>{item}</checkbox>\n      {/each}\n    </box>\n  {/each}\n  <button block variant=\"outline\" onClick={()=>GenUI.copy(checks.map(s=>s.section+\"\\n\"+s.items.map(i=>(done.includes(i)?\"[x] \":\"[ ] \")+i).join(\"\\n\")).join(\"\\n\\n\"))}>Copy checklist</button>\n</box>\n\nDo not sign a booking form that makes your deposit non-refundable before you have reviewed the material documents and total price. Have a lawyer who represents you, rather than the developer, review the agreement.\n\n## 10. Elite X versus a ready-to-move flat in Noida\n\nFor your specific requirements, this is the trade-off.\n\n| Factor | Elite X | Ready-to-move 3BHK in Noida |\n|---|---|---|\n| Move-in timing | RERA date is December 2028, beyond your target | Can potentially move in immediately after due diligence |\n| Budget | Advertised starting price is already above ₹2 crore | More room to compare total costs across existing properties |\n| Apartment condition | New construction; final execution remains to be seen | You can inspect the actual apartment and society |\n| Amenities | Planned modern amenities | Existing amenities and maintenance quality can be assessed |\n| Open space | Marketing claims approximately 69% open area | Actual greens and tower spacing can be inspected |\n| Commute to Sector 63 | Must be tested at peak hours | Can compare specific sectors and actual driving routes |\n| Main risk | Delivery, final specifications and cost escalation | Building age, maintenance, resale condition and society finances |\n\nElite X's biggest advantage is the prospect of a new home with modern amenities and planned open spaces. A completed flat's biggest advantage is that you can see what you are buying and avoid depending on future construction delivery.\n\nNeither option automatically offers better appreciation or resale value.\n\n## My final verdict\n\n<box border radius=\"lg\" padding={3} gap={2}>\n  <row align=\"center\" gap={2}>\n    <icon name=\"circle-alert\" size=\"xl\" color=\"warning\"/>\n    <title size=\"lg\">Conditional shortlist, not a booking recommendation</title>\n  </row>\n  Elite X may suit someone who prioritises a new high-rise, modern amenities and a larger advertised apartment. However, **it does not currently line up neatly with your ₹2 crore all-in budget or your October 2028 move-in target.**\n</box>\n\nI would proceed only if the developer provides a genuinely affordable written offer, your lawyer clears the documentation, and the construction and possession evidence support your deadline. Otherwise, I would prioritise ready-to-move 3BHKs in Noida that provide a practical commute to Sector 63, usable green space and a well-maintained society.\n\nOne last thing: I would not choose Elite X solely because it is new or because the marketing promises future connectivity. Your family's day-to-day experience and the total money committed matter more than either claim.\n\n**The next step I recommend:** obtain the current price sheet and tower-wise construction update, then compare Elite X with three ready-to-move societies in Noida using the same all-in budget and commute test. That will make the decision much clearer."

                        "1": "My initial view: ",
                        "2": "Elite X is worth investigating, but I would not book it without resolving three things first: the all-inclusive price, the possession timeline, and whether its location makes sense for your daily life.",
                        "3": "For your situation, this isn't just an investment decision. Visit at school opening and closing times, and inspect the approach roads and pedestrian access.\n\ngenui{\"map_widget_v2\":{\"points\":[{\"address\":\"Plot GH-03A, Sector 10, Greater Noida West, Uttar Pradesh\",\"name\":\"Elite X\",\"icon\":\"🏠\",\"id\":\"elite\"},{\"ref\":\"turn554236business1\",\"icon\":\"🎓\"},{\"ref\":\"turn554236business4\",\"icon\":\"🎓\"},{\"ref\":\"turn554236business0\",\"icon\":\"🏥\"}],\"carousel\":{\"visibility\":\"hidden\"},\"title\":\"Elite X and nearby facilities\",\"show_route\":false}}\n\n## 7\\. Open space, amenities and density\n\nElite X is marketed as a 5.44-acre project with approximately 69% open area, along with a swimming pool, fitness facilities, landscaped areas and other community amenities. citeturn554236search1turn554236search2\n\nThat sounds attractive for family living. But there are three things I would check before treating it as a genuine advantage.\n\n- **Usable greens\\:** does the open area include landscaped podiums, circulation areas, setbacks or spaces that cannot be used freely?\n- **Density\\:** the RERA-derived project data indicates hundreds of apartments across multiple high-rise towers. Check the actual number of units per floor, lifts per tower and expected parking demand. citeturn554236search3turn554236search4\n- **Maintenance\\:** ask for the estimated monthly maintenance rate per square foot, the services covered, and the proposed sinking fund or maintenance deposit.\n\nVisit the site and ask to see the approved master plan. Look for the distance between towers, afternoon shade, road noise, the location of the commercial area and whether the main greens are visible from the apartment you intend to buy.\n\nDo not assume that a large open-area percentage automatically means more quiet, privacy or usable garden space.\n\n## 8\\. Is Elite Group a reliable builder?\n\nThe developer behind Elite X is Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd. Elite Group's marketing materials identify earlier projects including Elite Homz in Sector 77 and Elite Golfgreens in Sector 79, Noida. citeturn554236search1turn554236search16\n\nThat gives you projects to investigate, but it does not establish the builder's delivery record or construction quality.\n\nBefore paying a booking amount, investigate\\:\n\n- **Possession history\\:** when were earlier projects actually handed over compared with their promised dates?\n- **Construction quality\\:** inspect completed buildings, common areas, basements, lifts, plumbing, waterproofing and finishing.\n- **Resident feedback\\:** speak directly to residents and maintenance staff, rather than relying exclusively on online ratings.\n- **Legal disputes\\:** check for pending material litigation, regulatory orders and land-related issues.\n- **Financial health\\:** have a property lawyer or qualified professional review the promoter, project charges, encumbrances and relevant disclosures.\n\nA registered project is not automatically free of legal or delivery risks. Equally, the existence of a complaint is not proof of wrongdoing. Look for documented evidence and patterns.\n\n## 9\\. Legal and financial checks before booking\n\nUse this as your booking checklist.\n\n## Booking due diligence\n\n(/ checked)\n\n[Copy checklist]\n\nDo not sign a booking form that makes your deposit non-refundable before you have reviewed the material documents and total price. Have a lawyer who represents you, rather than the developer, review the agreement.\n\n## 10\\. Elite X versus a ready-to-move flat in Noida\n\nFor your specific requirements, this is the trade-off.\n\n| Factor | Elite X | Ready-to-move 3BHK in Noida |\n|--------|--------|--------|\n| Move-in timing | RERA date is December 2028, beyond your target | Can potentially move in immediately after due diligence |\n| Budget | Advertised starting price is already above ₹2 crore | More room to compare total costs across existing properties |\n| Apartment condition | New construction; final execution remains to be seen | You can inspect the actual apartment and society |\n| Amenities | Planned modern amenities | Existing amenities and maintenance quality can be assessed |\n| Open space | Marketing claims approximately 69% open area | Actual greens and tower spacing can be inspected |\n| Commute to Sector 63 | Must be tested at peak hours | Can compare specific sectors and actual driving routes |\n| Main risk | Delivery, final specifications and cost escalation | Building age, maintenance, resale condition and society finances |\n\nElite X's biggest advantage is the prospect of a new home with modern amenities and planned open spaces. A completed flat's biggest advantage is that you can see what you are buying and avoid depending on future construction delivery.\n\nNeither option automatically offers better appreciation or resale value.\n\n## My final verdict\n\n## Conditional shortlist, not a booking recommendation\n\nElite X may suit someone who prioritises a new high-rise, modern amenities and a larger advertised apartment. However, **it does not currently line up neatly with your ₹2 crore all-in budget or your October 2028 move-in target.**\n\nI would proceed only if the developer provides a genuinely affordable written offer, your lawyer clears the documentation, and the construction and possession evidence support your deadline. Otherwise, I would prioritise ready-to-move 3BHKs in Noida that provide a practical commute to Sector 63, usable green space and a well-maintained society.\n\nOne last thing: I would not choose Elite X solely because it is new or because the marketing promises future connectivity. Your family's day-to-day experience and the total money committed matter more than either claim.\n\n**The next step I recommend\\:** obtain the current price sheet and tower-wise construction update, then compare Elite X with three ready-to-move societies in Noida using the same all-in budget and commute test.                                         "enriched_description": "Elite X is an under-construction premium residential high-rise project in Sector 10, Greater Noida West (Noida Extension), promoted by Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd. under the “Elite Group” brand. The project is registered with UP-RERA (Registration No. UPRERAPRJ916631/02/2024), with a declared completion date of 12-Dec-2028 and registration date 24-Feb-2024. \n\nProject overview (what it is)\n- Format & scale: The official project details describe six towers (G+25 to G+28) on about 5.44 acres, with 630 homes and relatively low ground coverage (27.6%), positioning the balance of the site as open/green areas. \n- Status & progress: The developer’s construction update states the structure was ~42% complete as of July 2026, with possession targeted in 2028 (aligned with the RERA completion timeline). \n\nHomes, layouts, and configurations\nElite X is marketed primarily as large-format 3 and 4 bedroom apartments, with multiple variants:\n- 3 BHK Residence: Super built-up 1,800–1,860 sq ft (variants 1,800 / 1,812 / 1,860), configured as 3 BHK + 3 toilets + entrance foyer; typically includes 3 balconies + 1 utility balcony. Starting price on the official site is ₹2.10 Cr onwards (excluding GST). \n- 3 BHK + Study: Super built-up 2,075–2,110 sq ft (variants 2,075 / 2,090 / 2,110), configured as 3 BHK + 3 toilets + 1 study + entrance foyer; typically includes 4 balconies + 1 utility balcony. Starting price on the official site is ₹2.42 Cr onwards (excluding GST). \n- 4 BHK + Servant Quarters: Super built-up 2,632–2,638 sq ft (variants 2,632 / 2,638), configured as 4 BHK + 4 toilets + 1 study + entrance foyer, with balconies on multiple sides plus a utility balcony. Starting price on the official site is ₹3.14 Cr onwards (excluding GST). \n\nAmenities and on-site lifestyle offering\nThe project’s amenity pitch is broad and “club-led,” with both leisure and practical conveniences:\n- Core highlighted amenities: elevated swimming pool, water feature & cabanas, fitness club, restaurant, banquet hall, and badminton court. \n- Family and community spaces: kids play area, reading zone, amphitheatre, party lawn, chess court, mini theatre, guest rooms, hobby studio, landscaped greens, open lawn, and arrival/drop-off zones. \n- Convenience: an on-site commercial plaza is shown as part of the development concept. \n- Safety & parking: “3-tier security” is repeatedly emphasized in the project’s marketing, along with dedicated parking. \n\nConstruction, specifications, and “fit-and-finish” positioning\nElite X positions itself as a premium-spec project with named-brand tie-ins and a modern high-rise specification set:\n- Structure & durability: earthquake-resistant RCC framed structure (latest seismic code), noted as approved by IIT or equivalent authorities (as per developer specs). \n- Flooring & finishes: premium vitrified tiles; anti-skid ceramic in kitchen/toilets/balconies; marble/Kota stone on staircases/landings; POP finish and internal paint details are listed in the specification section. \n- Doors/windows & utilities: hardwood main entrance door, UPVC sliding doors, aluminium composite windows; concealed conduits with fire-resistant copper wiring; modular switches; telephone/TV points; audio intercom “with security provision.” \n- Power & water: 100% DG power backup for common areas, plus underground/overhead water tanks for uninterrupted supply (as specified). \n- Branded components: the official site highlights brands such as Simpolo/Kajaria (tiles), Jaquar (CP fittings), Encraft (doors/windows), Supreme/Astral (plumbing), Polycab (wiring), Legrand (switches/MCBs), Mitsubishi Electric (air conditioning), and Schindler (lifts). \n\nLocation, connectivity, and nearby facilities\nElite X is located in Sector 10, Greater Noida West, positioned as an “emerging luxury address” with road and regional connectivity.\n- Macro connectivity claims: the project is described as ~3 minutes from NH-9, with connectivity toward Noida/Delhi and the Yamuna Expressway; the site also references Noida International Airport (Jewar) at ~55 km. \n- Nearby facilities listed by the developer: Gaur City Mall (~14 mins / 8.1 km), Arogya Hospital (~6 mins / 3.2 km), KDGS Hospital Sector 10 (~2 mins / 0.8 km), GD Goenka International School (~5 mins / 2.1 km), and Ghaziabad Railway Station (~30 mins / 16 km). \n- Upcoming infrastructure highlighted: FNG Expressway (~3 km, under construction) and Delhi–Meerut RRTS Rapid Rail (~20 km, under construction). \n\nDeveloper / promoter transparency and regulatory details\n- RERA: UP-RERA project summary lists “Elite X” with Registration No. UPRERAPRJ916631/02/2024, project type “New,” proposed start date 05-Jan-2024, and declared completion 12-Dec-2028; promoter is Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd. \n- Project address per official/RERA: Plot No. GH-03A, Sector 10, Greater Noida West (UP) 203207. \n\nWhat reviews commonly highlight (from available Google reviews)\nFrom the review snippets available in the provided records (53 reviews; overall rating 4.7/5), recurring themes are:\n- Location & accessibility: multiple reviewers call out the “prime” or “excellent” location, with one highlight stating “fantastic location.”\n- Layout, openness, and ventilation: reviewers mention a “three-side open plot,” a surrounding green belt, “massive open green areas,” and “next-level ventilation.”\n- Amenities & luxury positioning: repeated praise for “top-class luxury amenities” and “excellent amenities,” with expectations set by the sales team.\n- Sales/support experience: at least one reviewer specifically notes the sales team was “professional and supportive throughout the process.”\n\nBalanced considerations (practical notes for buyers)\n- Under-construction realities: timelines, specifications, and amenity delivery are subject to construction progress and approvals; the developer’s own specification section notes specifications are tentative and may change. \n- Due diligence: prospective buyers typically benefit from verifying the UP-RERA project details, construction updates, tower-wise plans, and the exact inclusions/exclusions (GST, parking, club charges, IFMS/maintenance, etc.) in the agreement for sale.\n\nOverall, Elite X presents itself as a large, premium high-rise community in Sector 10, Greater Noida West, with bigger unit sizes (3BHK/4BHK), extensive amenity programming (including a commercial plaza and multiple community spaces), and a strong emphasis on branded fittings, security, and “open green” planning—while remaining a project where delivery and final specifications should be evaluated against the latest RERA disclosures and on-site progress updates.",

        {
            "id": "a152d51a-9134-490b-bbde-fb0de8a724ae",
            "author": {
                "role": "assistant",

            "create_time": 1792071930.923403,
            "update_time": 1792071944.180749,
            "content": {
                "content_type": "text",
                "parts": [
                    "# Elite X's builder: background, delivery record and legal risks\n\nThe company behind Elite X is **Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd., which markets its residential projects under the Elite Group name.** My research found one documented possession-date extension on its earlier project, Elite Golfgreens, and legal proceedings involving the company. These deserve scrutiny before you commit ₹2 crore to Elite X.\n\nThe important distinction is that a delay or court case involving a builder is not automatically proof that its current project is unsafe. We need to look at the specific project, dates and court orders.\n\n## 1. Who is the builder?\n\n<row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n  <AsyncImage query=\"Elite Group Noida Elite Golfgreens residential apartment building completed project\" aspectRatio=\"4:5\" maxWidth=\"124px\"/>\n  <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n    <title size=\"lg\"><Entity value=\"Elite Group\" category=\"brand\" disambig=\"Residential real estate developer in Noida NCR\"/></title>\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Brand and marketing name</text>\n    <title size=\"md\"><Entity value=\"Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd.\" category=\"company\"/></title>\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Legal promoter named in Elite X's RERA registration</text>\n    Elite X is registered under UP-RERA number UPRERAPRJ916631/02/2024, with a declared completion date of 12 December 2028. <Cite refs={[\"turn686304view0\",\"turn783240search7\"]}/>\n  </box>\n</row>\n\nThe company's registered promoter details are available through the <Entity value=\"Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority\" category=\"organization\"/>. Its public project record lists two projects under the promoter, with one complaint recorded across those projects as of the displayed record. <Cite refs={[\"turn686304view0\",\"turn686304search1\"]}/>\n\nOfficial verification: <Link url=\"https://www.up-rera.in/\" title=\"UP-RERA website\"/>.\n\n## 2. Which projects have they completed?\n\nThe developer identifies two earlier residential projects in Noida.\n\n<box gap={3}>\n  <row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n    <AsyncImage query=\"Elite Homz Sector 77 Noida completed residential society apartment towers\" aspectRatio=\"4:5\" maxWidth=\"124px\"/>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      **Elite Homz — Sector 77, Noida**\n\n      <badge color=\"success\">Reported delivered</badge>\n\n      - Approximately 572 homes.\n      - The developer reports handover in 2015.\n      - This is the earlier project I would inspect first for construction quality, maintenance and resident feedback.\n\n      <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Source: developer's portfolio. <Cite refs={[\"turn783240search7\",\"turn783240search10\"]}/></text>\n    </box>\n  </row>\n  <divider color=\"subtle\"/>\n  <row align=\"start\" gap={3}>\n    <AsyncImage query=\"Elite Golf Greens Sector 79 Noida completed residential society towers landscaping\" aspectRatio=\"4:5\" maxWidth=\"124px\"/>\n    <box flex=\"1\" gap={1}>\n      **Elite Golfgreens — Sector 79, Noida**\n\n      <badge color=\"warning\">Completion-date extension recorded</badge>\n\n      - A residential development registered under UP-RERA in July 2017.\n      - The original declared completion date was 10 June 2021.\n      - The RERA record shows an extension to 4 May 2022, approximately 328 days later.\n\n      <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">Sources: official UP-RERA project summary and registration records. <Cite refs={[\"turn783240search9\",\"turn686304search3\",\"turn783240search5\"]}/></text>\n    </box>\n  </row>\n</box>\n\nThe distinction matters: Elite Golfgreens has a documented delay against its registered completion date. The developer says it was handed over in 2021, but that claim conflicts with the registered extension to May 2022. I would not treat the marketing statement as proof of timely delivery.\n\nBefore judging the quality of the finished project, visit both societies and speak to residents who bought directly from the developer.\n\n## 3. Have they faced possession delays?\n\n**Yes. There is a documented completion-date extension for Elite Golfgreens.**\n\n<box border radius=\"lg\" padding={3} gap={3}>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Original deadline</text>\n    <title size=\"md\">10 Jun 2021</title>\n  </row>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Revised deadline</text>\n    <title size=\"md\">4 May 2022</title>\n  </row>\n  <divider/>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Recorded extension</text>\n    <title size=\"lg\" color=\"warning\">328 days</title>\n  </row>\n  <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"xs\">The extension is recorded in UP-RERA's project information. It does not, by itself, establish when every buyer received possession or why the extension was granted. <Cite refs={[\"turn783240search9\",\"turn686304search3\"]}/></text>\n</box>\n\nFor Elite X, the registered completion date is 12 December 2028. I would therefore treat timely delivery as an **unproven risk**, rather than assume that the builder will finish on schedule.\n\nThere is also a difference between a completion-date extension granted by RERA and an actual delay beyond the revised deadline. The former is documented here; the latter needs to be established from possession records and individual buyer agreements.\n\n## 4. Have they faced legal disputes?\n\nMy search found two matters worth distinguishing.\n\n### A. Delhi High Court proceedings involving Golfgreen Mansions\n\nA Delhi High Court order dated 27 August 2025 in *Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd. v. Kinetic Buildtech Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.* records a commercial dispute concerning contractual obligations and the transfer or encumbrance of property.\n\nThe court granted interim protection, including directions to maintain the status quo regarding shareholding and directorship and a restraint against alienating or encumbering a particular property, Plot GH-3B, Sector 10, Greater Noida, pending the next hearing. <Cite refs={[\"turn686304search6\"]}/>\n\n**Why this matters:** the case involves the same promoter and a property in Sector 10, so it warrants a closer legal check.\n\n**What it does not establish:** the order concerns Plot GH-3B, whereas Elite X is registered at Plot GH-03A. I have not established that the property in that dispute is the Elite X project land. Nor does an interim order establish that the promoter has committed wrongdoing.\n\nBefore booking, ask your independent lawyer to check the case's subsequent orders and whether any agreement, land interest, financing arrangement or party involved overlaps with Elite X.\n\n### B. UP-RERA buyer complaints\n\nThe public promoter record shows one complaint across the promoter's two registered projects, with zero complaints recorded against Elite X in the retrieved record. <Cite refs={[\"turn686304view0\",\"turn686304search1\"]}/>\n\nThat is useful, but it is not a clean bill of health. Elite X is still under construction, and a low complaint count does not measure construction quality, future delivery performance or disputes that have not been filed with RERA.\n\nI have not established a complete, verified inventory of every civil, consumer, criminal or commercial proceeding involving the company or its directors. The findings above should not be read as an exhaustive litigation search.\n\n## 5. My risk assessment for your purchase\n\n| Issue | Assessment |\n|---|---|\n| Previous delivery record | One recorded completion-date extension |\n| Completed-project experience | Two earlier projects identified by the developer; inspect them independently |\n| Elite X RERA registration | Verified in the public registration record |\n| Complaints against Elite X | Zero in the retrieved RERA record |\n| Legal proceedings | A documented High Court commercial dispute involving the promoter; connection to Elite X land not established |\n| Delivery by your target of October 2028 | Not established; the registered date is December 2028 |\n\n## 6. What I would demand before paying a booking amount\n\n1. **A written possession commitment** that addresses your October 2028 deadline and the consequences of delay.\n2. **A fresh construction-progress report** and an independent site inspection.\n3. **A legal title and encumbrance report** for Plot GH-03A specifically, including any mortgages, charges, litigation and authority dues.\n4. **The latest status of the Kinetic Buildtech litigation**, reviewed by your own property lawyer.\n5. **Direct feedback from residents of Elite Homz and Elite Golfgreens**, particularly buyers who experienced handover and maintenance.\n6. **A signed all-inclusive cost sheet** for your exact 3BHK, including applicable taxes, parking, registration, maintenance deposits and other charges.\n\nMy conclusion is not that Elite Group is an unsafe builder. It is that the available record shows a real delivery-date extension and a legal matter that deserves verification. Given your budget and move-in deadline, I would not rely on the developer's marketing claims alone.\n\n**The single most useful next step is to inspect Elite Golfgreens in person and speak to at least three residents who bought directly from the builder.** Ask them when they received possession, whether the final charges matched the original quotation, and how the builder handled defects after handover. Those answers will help you judge Elite X more accurately than the brochure will."
                ]
            },

Which projects have they completed?\n\nThe developer identifies two earlier residential projects in Noida.\n\nimage_group{\"query\":[\"Elite Homz Sector 77 Noida completed residential society apartment towers\"],\"aspect_ratio\":\"4:5\",\"layout\":\"carousel\",\"num_per_query\":1}\n\n**Elite Homz — Sector 77, Noida**\n\n(Reported delivered)\n\n- Approximately 572 homes.\n- The developer reports handover in 2015.\n- This is the earlier project I would inspect first for construction quality, maintenance and resident feedback.\n\nSource: developer's portfolio. citeturn783240search7turn783240search10\n\n---\n\nimage_group{\"query\":[\"Elite Golf Greens Sector 79 Noida completed residential society towers landscaping\"],\"aspect_ratio\":\"4:5\",\"layout\":\"carousel\",\"num_per_query\":1}\n\n**Elite Golfgreens — Sector 79, Noida**\n\n(Completion-date extension recorded)\n\n- A residential development registered under UP-RERA in July 2017.\n- The original declared completion date was 10 June 2021.\n- The RERA record shows an extension to 4 May 2022, approximately 328 days later.\n\nSources: official UP-RERA project summary and registration records. citeturn783240search9turn686304search3turn783240search5\n\nThe distinction matters: Elite Golfgreens has a documented delay against its registered completion date. The developer says it was handed over in 2021, but that claim conflicts with the registered extension to May 2022. I would not treat the marketing statement as proof of timely delivery.\n\nBefore judging the quality of the finished project, visit both societies and speak to residents who bought directly from the developer.\n\n## 3\\. Have they faced possession delays?\n\n**Yes. There is a documented completion-date extension for Elite Golfgreens.**\n\nOriginal deadline\n\n### 10 Jun 2021\n\nRevised deadline\n\n### 4 May 2022\n\n---\n\nRecorded extension\n\n## 328 days\n\nThe extension is recorded in UP-RERA's project information. It does not, by itself, establish when every buyer received possession or why the extension was granted. citeturn783240search9turn686304search3\n\nFor Elite X, the registered completion date is 12 December 2028. I would therefore treat timely delivery as an **unproven risk**, rather than assume that the builder will finish on schedule.\n\nThere is also a difference between a completion-date extension granted by RERA and an actual delay beyond the revised deadline. The former is documented here; the latter needs to be established from possession records and individual buyer agreements.\n\n## 4\\. Have they faced legal disputes?\n\nMy search found two matters worth distinguishing.\n\n### A. Delhi High Court proceedings involving Golfgreen Mansions\n\nA Delhi High Court order dated 27 August 2025 in *Golfgreen Mansions Pvt. Ltd. v. Kinetic Buildtech Pvt. Ltd. &amp; Ors.* records a commercial dispute concerning contractual obligations and the transfer or encumbrance of property.\n\nThe court granted interim protection, including directions to maintain the status quo regarding shareholding and directorship and a restraint against alienating or encumbering a particular property, Plot GH-3B, Sector 10, Greater Noida, pending the next hearing. citeturn686304search6\n\n**Why this matters\\:** the case involves the same promoter and a property in Sector 10, so it warrants a closer legal check.\n\n**What it does not establish\\:** the order concerns Plot GH-3B, whereas Elite X is registered at Plot GH-03A. I have not established that the property in that dispute is the Elite X project land. Nor does an interim order establish that the promoter has committed wrongdoing.\n\nBefore booking, ask your independent lawyer to check the case's subsequent orders and whether any agreement, land interest, financing arrangement or party involved overlaps with Elite X.\n\n### B. UP-RERA buyer complaints\n\nThe public promoter record shows one complaint across the promoter's two registered projects, with zero complaints recorded against Elite X in the retrieved record. citeturn686304view0turn686304search1\n\nThat is useful, but it is not a clean bill of health. Elite X is still under construction, and a low complaint count does not measure construction quality, future delivery performance or disputes that have not been filed with RERA.\n\nI have not established a complete, verified inventory of every civil, consumer, criminal or commercial proceeding involving the company or its directors. The findings above should not be read as an exhaustive litigation search.\n\n## 5\\. My risk assessment for your purchase\n\n| Issue | Assessment |\n|--------|--------|\n| Previous delivery record | One recorded completion-date extension |\n| Completed-project experience | Two earlier projects identified by the developer; inspect them independently |\n| Elite X RERA registration | Verified in the public registration record |\n| Complaints against Elite X | Zero in the retrieved RERA record |\n| Legal proceedings | A documented High Court commercial dispute involving the promoter; connection to Elite X land not established |\n| Delivery by your target of October 2028 | Not established; the registered date is December 2028 |\n\n## 6\\. What I would demand before paying a booking amount\n\n1. **A written possession commitment** that addresses your October 2028 deadline and the consequences of delay.\n2. **A fresh construction-progress report** and an independent site inspection.\n3. **A legal title and encumbrance report** for Plot GH-03A specifically, including any mortgages, charges, litigation and authority dues.\n4. **The latest status of the Kinetic Buildtech litigation**, reviewed by your own property lawyer.\n5. **Direct feedback from residents of Elite Homz and Elite Golfgreens**, particularly buyers who experienced handover and maintenance.\n6. **A signed all-inclusive cost sheet** for your exact 3BHK, including applicable taxes, parking, registration, maintenance deposits and other charges.\n\nMy conclusion is not that Elite Group is an unsafe builder. It is that the available record shows a real delivery-date extension and a legal matter that deserves verification. Given your budget and move-in deadline, I would not rely on the developer's marketing claims alone.\n\n**The single most useful next step is to inspect Elite Golfgreens in person and speak to at least three residents who bought directly from the builder.** Ask them when they received possession, whether the final charges matched the original quotation, and how the builder handled defects after handover. Those answers will help you judge Elite X more accurately than the brochure will.",

                                "url": "https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/noida/strange-that-homebuyers-who-have-paid-in-full-cant-register-flats-because-of-govt-builder-dispute-hc/articleshow/134950768.cms",
                                "title": "Strange that homebuyers who have paid in full can't register flats because of govt-builder dispute: Allahabad high court",
                                "snippet": "The Allahabad High Court has expressed concern over the situation where fully paid homebuyers are unable to register their flats due to a dispute between the builder and government agencies. The issue was highlighted in a plea filed by residents of Ajnara Homes in Greater Noida West. The court found it \"strange\" that buyers who fulfilled their financial obligations are being penalized because the real estate developer has failed to clear its dues to government bodies. In response, the court has directed the state government, Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority, and the Uttar Pradesh Real Estate Regulatory Authority (UP-RERA) to provide a clear plan of action to address this issue. The case underscores the continuing problems faced by homebuyers in India due to regulatory and developer-related delays.",

        {
            "id": "e37d5daf-1f3f-42dc-a42f-96b4b3cb7842",
            "author": {
                "role": "assistant",
                "name": null,
                "metadata": {}
            },
            "create_time": 1792071959.959938,
            "update_time": 1792071987.110435,
            "content": {
                "content_type": "text",
                "parts": [
                    "# Elite X payment plans: which one is safer?\n\nFor your 3BHK purchase, **I would generally prefer a genuine construction-linked payment plan over a plan that asks you to pay a large amount upfront in exchange for easier initial instalments later.**\n\nBut there's an important distinction: a plan with a small booking amount isn't necessarily safer. What matters is *when the remaining money becomes payable, what triggers each payment, and what happens if construction is delayed.*\n\nFor Elite X, we have previously encountered a publicly listed payment schedule of 10% at booking, 40% within 45 days, 20% at structure completion, 20% at external painting, and a final 10% whose milestone needs clarification. I have not verified that this is the developer's current, official offer, so treat it as a schedule to investigate rather than a confirmed plan.\n\nGiven your ₹2 crore all-in budget and your goal of moving in by October 2028, the payment plan also needs to protect your cash flow without locking too much of your money into a project whose RERA completion date is 12 December 2028.\n\n## 1. What payment plans are listed for Elite X?\n\nI found a third-party listing from Invest Mango showing the following schedule. The developer's official website offers a price list on request but does not publish this payment schedule on the page I checked. Therefore, ask Golfgreen Mansions to confirm whether it is currently available for your specific 3BHK. <Cite refs={[\"turn370122view0\",\"turn370122view1\"]}/>\n\n| Payment milestone | Share of base price |\n|---|---:|\n| Booking | 10% |\n| Within 60 days of booking | 30% |\n| Casting of second basement roof | 7.5% |\n| Casting of sixth-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Casting of twelfth-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Casting of eighteenth-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Casting of twenty-fourth-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Casting of top-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Flooring | 10% |\n| Offer of possession | 5% |\n| **Total** | **100%** |\n\n<text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Source: third-party Elite X payment-plan listing. These milestones and percentages have not been confirmed against a current signed developer offer. <Cite refs={[\"turn370122view0\"]}/></text>\n\nThe key issue is the second instalment. You would pay **40% of the base price within 60 days**, even though the later payments are linked to construction milestones.\n\nThat makes this a relatively front-loaded schedule, not the evenly spread construction-linked plan many buyers imagine.\n\n### What would that mean in rupees?\n\n<box border radius=\"xl\" padding={3} gap={3}>\n  <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Illustration using your previously quoted ₹1.85 crore base price</text>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <text>At booking (10%)</text>\n    <title size=\"lg\">₹18.5 lakh</title>\n  </row>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <text>Within 60 days (30%)</text>\n    <title size=\"lg\">₹55.5 lakh</title>\n  </row>\n  <divider/>\n  <row align=\"center\" justify=\"between\">\n    <text>**Total within 60 days**</text>\n    <title size=\"xl\" color=\"warning\">₹74 lakh</title>\n  </row>\n  <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">This excludes taxes, stamp duty, registration and other charges. It is a calculation based on the illustrative base price, not a current quote.</text>\n</box>\n\nIf the base price is instead ₹2.10 crore, 40% would be ₹84 lakh. Either way, this schedule requires substantial early funding.\n\n## 2. Construction-linked versus low-initial-payment plans\n\n<box border radius=\"xl\" padding={3} gap={3}>\n  <box gap={1}>\n    <title size=\"lg\">Option A: Construction-linked plan (CLP)</title>\n    <badge color=\"success\">Generally preferred</badge>\n    You pay instalments as agreed construction stages are completed. If the milestones are genuine, documented and independently verifiable, your payments broadly track the work being done.\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Main risk: the plan may still demand a large amount early, or use vague milestones.</text>\n  </box>\n  <divider/>\n  <box gap={1}>\n    <title size=\"lg\">Option B: Down-payment plan</title>\n    You pay a large proportion of the price shortly after booking, sometimes in exchange for a discount.\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Main risk: more of your money is exposed to the developer before the corresponding construction is completed. A discount may not compensate for that risk.</text>\n  </box>\n  <divider/>\n  <box gap={1}>\n    <title size=\"lg\">Option C: Low-booking or 10:90 plan</title>\n    You pay a small initial percentage and most of the balance later, commonly around possession under a genuine 10:90 structure.\n    <text color=\"secondary\" size=\"sm\">Main risk: the remaining amount can be large, and you must check the price premium, possession conditions, financing arrangements and what happens if delivery is delayed.</text>\n  </box>\n</box>\n\nA low booking amount can help you preserve cash, but it does not automatically make the deal safer. Some plans defer payment without protecting you against delay; others may carry a higher price or special contractual conditions.\n\nFor a home under construction, I would choose the plan that ties the largest possible share of payments to **verifiable physical progress**, keeps a reasonable amount due at possession, and does not require you to pay far ahead of the construction.\n\n## 3. A legal safeguard before paying\n\nUP-RERA has specifically reminded buyers and developers that **no more than 10% of the unit price should be collected before a written agreement for sale has been executed and registered**. The agreement should set out the payment schedule and possession date. <Cite refs={[\"turn197190search13\",\"turn197190search11\"]}/>\n\nSo, if Elite X asks for 10% at booking and another 30% within 60 days, ask for the registered agreement before paying beyond the permitted booking amount. Have a property lawyer review the agreement and confirm the precise payment obligations.\n\nAlso, pay only to the verified project collection account and obtain receipts for every payment.\n\n## 4. What I would negotiate with Elite X\n\nI would ask the sales team for three written alternatives for the same apartment:\n\n- **Plan A:** a construction-linked schedule with instalments distributed across independently verifiable construction stages.\n- **Plan B:** a low-initial-payment plan, with the deferred amount and all conditions clearly specified.\n- **Plan C:** the largest-upfront-payment plan, including the exact discount against the other two.\n\nCompare the *total price*, not just the payment dates. Ask whether any discount disappears if you change plans, whether the quoted price includes the same charges, and whether the final instalment depends on an actual possession offer or merely a construction milestone.\n\nFor every construction-linked demand, insist on the milestone specified in the registered agreement and supporting evidence that the work has reached that stage.\n\n## My recommendation for you\n\nGiven Elite X's delivery timeline and the previous completion-date extension recorded for the builder's earlier project, I would **not pay 40% within 60 days simply to secure the apartment**. I would negotiate a more evenly spread construction-linked plan, with a meaningful balance payable at possession.\n\nIf the builder refuses and your only options require substantial early payment, I would reconsider the purchase rather than let an attractive payment offer distract from the delivery risk.\n\nOne point remains especially important: your ₹2 crore budget is meant to cover the whole purchase, not just the base price. A payment plan can spread the cost over time, but it cannot make an unaffordable apartment affordable.\n\n"
                ]

                        "0": "Elite X payment plans: which one is safer?",
                        "1": "For your 3BHK purchase, ",
                        "2": "I would generally prefer a genuine construction-linked payment plan over a plan that asks you to pay a large amount upfront in exchange for easier initial instalments later.",
                        "3": "But there's an important distinction: a plan with a small booking amount isn't necessarily safer. What matters is ",
                        "4": "when the remaining money becomes payable, what triggers each payment, and what happens if construction is delayed.",
                        "5": "For Elite X, we have previously encountered a publicly listed payment schedule of 10% at booking, 40% within 45 days, 20% at structure completion, 20% at external painting, and a final 10% whose milestone needs clarification. I have not verified that this is the developer's current, official offer, so treat it as a schedule to investigate rather than a confirmed plan.",
                        "6": "Given your ₹2 crore all-in budget and your goal of moving in by October 2028, the payment plan also needs to protect your cash flow without locking too much of your money into a project whose RERA completion date is 12 December 2028.",
                        "7": "1. What payment plans are listed for Elite X?",
                        "8": "I found a third-party listing from Invest Mango showing the following schedule. The developer's official website offers a price list on request but does not publish this payment schedule on the page I checked. Therefore, ask Golfgreen Mansions to confirm whether it is currently available for your specific 3BHK. ",

                        "16": "30%",
                        "17": "Casting of second basement roof",
                        "18": "7.5%",
                        "19": "Casting of sixth-floor slab",
                        "20": "7.5%",

                        "22": "7.5%",
                        "23": "Casting of eighteenth-floor slab",
                        "24": "7.5%",
                        "25": "Casting of twenty-fourth-floor slab",
                        "26": "7.5%",

                        "28": "7.5%",
                        "29": "Flooring",

                        "31": "Offer of possession",
                        "32": "5%",
                        "33": "Total",
                        "34": "100%",
                        "35": "Source: third-party Elite X payment-plan listing. These milestones and percentages have not been confirmed against a current signed developer offer. ",

                        "37": "942d2c4a-6ecd-545a-a687-b8420b25b9e3",
                        "38": "The key issue is the second instalment. You would pay ",
                        "39": "40% of the base price within 60 days",
                        "40": ", even though the later payments are linked to construction milestones.",
                        "41": "That makes this a relatively front-loaded schedule, not the evenly spread construction-linked plan many buyers imagine.",
                        "42": "What would that mean in rupees?",
                        "43": "Illustration using your previously quoted ₹1.85 crore base price",
                        "44": "At booking (10%)",
                        "45": "₹18.5 lakh",
                        "46": "Within 60 days (30%)",
                        "47": "₹55.5 lakh",
                        "48": "Total within 60 days",
                        "49": "₹74 lakh",
                        "50": "This excludes taxes, stamp duty, registration and other charges. It is a calculation based on the illustrative base price, not a current quote.",
                        "51": "If the base price is instead ₹2.10 crore, 40% would be ₹84 lakh. Either way, this schedule requires substantial early funding.",
                        "52": "2. Construction-linked versus low-initial-payment plans",
                        "53": "Option A: Construction-linked plan (CLP)",
                        "54": "Generally preferred",
                        "55": "You pay instalments as agreed construction stages are completed. If the milestones are genuine, documented and independently verifiable, your payments broadly track the work being done.",
                        "56": "Main risk: the plan may still demand a large amount early, or use vague milestones.",
                        "57": "Option B: Down-payment plan",
                        "58": "You pay a large proportion of the price shortly after booking, sometimes in exchange for a discount.",
                        "59": "Main risk: more of your money is exposed to the developer before the corresponding construction is completed. A discount may not compensate for that risk.",
                        "60": "Option C: Low-booking or 10:90 plan",
                        "61": "You pay a small initial percentage and most of the balance later, commonly around possession under a genuine 10:90 structure.",
                        "62": "Main risk: the remaining amount can be large, and you must check the price premium, possession conditions, financing arrangements and what happens if delivery is delayed.",
                        "63": "A low booking amount can help you preserve cash, but it does not automatically make the deal safer. Some plans defer payment without protecting you against delay; others may carry a higher price or special contractual conditions.",
                        "64": "For a home under construction, I would choose the plan that ties the largest possible share of payments to ",
                        "65": "verifiable physical progress",
                        "66": ", keeps a reasonable amount due at possession, and does not require you to pay far ahead of the construction.",
                        "67": "3. A legal safeguard before paying",
                        "68": "UP-RERA has specifically reminded buyers and developers that ",
                        "69": "no more than 10% of the unit price should be collected before a written agreement for sale has been executed and registered",
                        "70": ". The agreement should set out the payment schedule and possession date. ",

                            "turn197190search11"

                        "72": "965e8727-dd6e-5984-99ee-d31eb3b63259",
                        "73": "So, if Elite X asks for 10% at booking and another 30% within 60 days, ask for the registered agreement before paying beyond the permitted booking amount. Have a property lawyer review the agreement and confirm the precise payment obligations.",
                        "74": "Also, pay only to the verified project collection account and obtain receipts for every payment.",
                        "75": "4. What I would negotiate with Elite X",
                        "76": "I would ask the sales team for three written alternatives for the same apartment:",
                        "77": "Plan A:",
                        "78": " a construction-linked schedule with instalments distributed across independently verifiable construction stages.",
                        "79": "Plan B:",
                        "80": " a low-initial-payment plan, with the deferred amount and all conditions clearly specified.",
                        "81": "Plan C:",
                        "82": " the largest-upfront-payment plan, including the exact discount against the other two.",
                        "83": "Compare the ",
                        "84": "total price",
                        "85": ", not just the payment dates. Ask whether any discount disappears if you change plans, whether the quoted price includes the same charges, and whether the final instalment depends on an actual possession offer or merely a construction milestone.",
                        "86": "For every construction-linked demand, insist on the milestone specified in the registered agreement and supporting evidence that the work has reached that stage.",
                        "87": "My recommendation for you",
                        "88": "Given Elite X's delivery timeline and the previous completion-date extension recorded for the builder's earlier project, I would ",
                        "89": "not pay 40% within 60 days simply to secure the apartment",
                        "90": ". I would negotiate a more evenly spread construction-linked plan, with a meaningful balance payable at possession.",
                        "91": "If the builder refuses and your only options require substantial early payment, I would reconsider the purchase rather than let an attractive payment offer distract from the delivery risk.",
                        "92": "One point remains especially important: your ₹2 crore budget is meant to cover the whole purchase, not just the base price. A payment plan can spread the cost over time, but it cannot make an unaffordable apartment affordable."

                    "fallbackMarkdown": "# Elite X payment plans: which one is safer?\n\nFor your 3BHK purchase, **I would generally prefer a genuine construction-linked payment plan over a plan that asks you to pay a large amount upfront in exchange for easier initial instalments later.**\n\nBut there's an important distinction: a plan with a small booking amount isn't necessarily safer. What matters is *when the remaining money becomes payable, what triggers each payment, and what happens if construction is delayed.*\n\nFor Elite X, we have previously encountered a publicly listed payment schedule of 10% at booking, 40% within 45 days, 20% at structure completion, 20% at external painting, and a final 10% whose milestone needs clarification. I have not verified that this is the developer's current, official offer, so treat it as a schedule to investigate rather than a confirmed plan.\n\nGiven your ₹2 crore all-in budget and your goal of moving in by October 2028, the payment plan also needs to protect your cash flow without locking too much of your money into a project whose RERA completion date is 12 December 2028.\n\n## 1\\. What payment plans are listed for Elite X?\n\nI found a third-party listing from Invest Mango showing the following schedule. The developer's official website offers a price list on request but does not publish this payment schedule on the page I checked. Therefore, ask Golfgreen Mansions to confirm whether it is currently available for your specific 3BHK. citeturn370122view0turn370122view1\n\n| Payment milestone | Share of base price |\n|--------|--------|\n| Booking | 10% |\n| Within 60 days of booking | 30% |\n| Casting of second basement roof | 7.5% |\n| Casting of sixth-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Casting of twelfth-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Casting of eighteenth-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Casting of twenty-fourth-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Casting of top-floor slab | 7.5% |\n| Flooring | 10% |\n| Offer of possession | 5% |\n| **Total** | **100%** |\n\nSource: third-party Elite X payment-plan listing. These milestones and percentages have not been confirmed against a current signed developer offer. citeturn370122view0\n\nThe key issue is the second instalment. You would pay **40% of the base price within 60 days**, even though the later payments are linked to construction milestones.\n\nThat makes this a relatively front-loaded schedule, not the evenly spread construction-linked plan many buyers imagine.\n\n### What would that mean in rupees?\n\nIllustration using your previously quoted ₹1.85 crore base price\n\nAt booking (10%)\n\n## ₹18.5 lakh\n\nWithin 60 days (30%)\n\n## ₹55.5 lakh\n\n---\n\n**Total within 60 days**\n\n# ₹74 lakh\n\nThis excludes taxes, stamp duty, registration and other charges. It is a calculation based on the illustrative base price, not a current quote.\n\nIf the base price is instead ₹2.10 crore, 40% would be ₹84 lakh. Either way, this schedule requires substantial early funding.\n\n## 2\\. Construction-linked versus low-initial-payment plans\n\n## Option A: Construction-linked plan (CLP)\n\n(Generally preferred)\n\nYou pay instalments as agreed construction stages are completed. If the milestones are genuine, documented and independently verifiable, your payments broadly track the work being done.\n\nMain risk: the plan may still demand a large amount early, or use vague milestones.\n\n---\n\n## Option B: Down-payment plan\n\nYou pay a large proportion of the price shortly after booking, sometimes in exchange for a discount.\n\nMain risk: more of your money is exposed to the developer before the corresponding construction is completed. A discount may not compensate for that risk.\n\n---\n\n## Option C: Low-booking or 10:90 plan\n\nYou pay a small initial percentage and most of the balance later, commonly around possession under a genuine 10:90 structure.\n\nMain risk: the remaining amount can be large, and you must check the price premium, possession conditions, financing arrangements and what happens if delivery is delayed.\n\nA low booking amount can help you preserve cash, but it does not automatically make the deal safer. Some plans defer payment without protecting you against delay; others may carry a higher price or special contractual conditions.\n\nFor a home under construction, I would choose the plan that ties the largest possible share of payments to **verifiable physical progress**, keeps a reasonable amount due at possession, and does not require you to pay far ahead of the construction.\n\n## 3\\. A legal safeguard before paying\n\nUP-RERA has specifically reminded buyers and developers that **no more than 10% of the unit price should be collected before a written agreement for sale has been executed and registered**\\. The agreement should set out the payment schedule and possession date. citeturn197190search13turn197190search11\n\nSo, if Elite X asks for 10% at booking and another 30% within 60 days, ask for the registered agreement before paying beyond the permitted booking amount. Have a property lawyer review the agreement and confirm the precise payment obligations.\n\nAlso, pay only to the verified project collection account and obtain receipts for every payment.\n\n## 4\\. What I would negotiate with Elite X\n\nI would ask the sales team for three written alternatives for the same apartment\\:\n\n- **Plan A\\:** a construction-linked schedule with instalments distributed across independently verifiable construction stages.\n- **Plan B\\:** a low-initial-payment plan, with the deferred amount and all conditions clearly specified.\n- **Plan C\\:** the largest-upfront-payment plan, including the exact discount against the other two.\n\nCompare the *total price*, not just the payment dates. Ask whether any discount disappears if you change plans, whether the quoted price includes the same charges, and whether the final instalment depends on an actual possession offer or merely a construction milestone.\n\nFor every construction-linked demand, insist on the milestone specified in the registered agreement and supporting evidence that the work has reached that stage.\n\n## My recommendation for you\n\nGiven Elite X's delivery timeline and the previous completion-date extension recorded for the builder's earlier project, I would **not pay 40% within 60 days simply to secure the apartment**\\. I would negotiate a more evenly spread construction-linked plan, with a meaningful balance payable at possession.\n\nIf the builder refuses and your only options require substantial early payment, I would reconsider the purchase rather than let an attractive payment offer distract from the delivery risk.\n\nOne point remains especially important: your ₹2 crore budget is meant to cover the whole purchase, not just the base price. A payment plan can spread the cost over time, but it cannot make an unaffordable apartment affordable.",
